notes.text: Then Peter standing up — All the gestures, all the words of Peter, show the utmost sobriety; lifted up his voice - With cheerfulness and boldness; and said to them - This discourse has three parts; each of which, ver. 14, 22, 29, begins with the same appellation, men: only to the last part he prefixes with more familiarity the additional word brethren. Men of Judea - That is, ye that are born in Judea. St. Peter spoke in Hebrew, which they all understood.

Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God — The apostle here anticipates an objection, Why did God suffer such a person to be so treated? Did he not know what wicked men intended to do? And had he not power to prevent it? Yea. He knew all that those wicked men intended to do. And he had power to blast all their designs in a moment. But he did not exert that power, because he so loved the world! Because it was the determined counsel of his love, to redeem mankind from eternal death, by the death of his only-begotten Son.
Having loosed the pains of death — The word properly means, the pains of a woman in travail. As it was not possible that he should be held under it - Because the Scripture must needs be fulfilled.
Psalm xvi, 8.

Thou wilt not leave my soul in hades — The invisible world. But it does not appear, that ever our Lord went into hell. His soul, when it was separated from the body, did not go thither, but to paradise, Luke xxiii, 43. The meaning is, Thou wilt not leave my soul in its separate state, nor suffer my body to be corrupted.
Thou hast made known to me the ways of life — That is, Thou hast raised me from the dead. Thou wilt fill me with joy by thy countenance - When I ascend to thy right hand.
The patriarch — A more honourable title than king.
Psalm lxxxix, 4, &c.

He foreseeing this, spake of the resurrection Of Christ — St. Peter argues thus: It is plain, David did not speak this of himself. Therefore he spake of Christ's rising. But how does that promise of a kingdom imply his resurrection? Because he did not receive it before he died, and because his kingdom was to endure forever, 2 Sam. vii, 13.

glossa.text: *Jewish men.* That is, there are two causes of prudence, namely that they were Jews, and that they dwelt in Jerusalem, which sobriety becomes.

*By the determinate counsel. ((RAB.))* In this alone were the Jews blameworthy, that they did it not with an obedient mind.

*And foreknowledge of God,* etc. ((ID.)) In the Greek it is thus: *Receiving him thus delivered up by foreknowledge.* For he was delivered by the governor into their power, that they might choose either him or the robber, but life being granted to the robber, they slew Jesus by the hands of the soldiers.

*He hath raised up.* Not by the resurrection usual with the rest and common, which is deferred to the end, but by that which was celebrated on the third day, that the assertion of this resurrection might be a testimony of the Deity.

((RAB.)) He raised up, according to the humanity, which the Jews most greatly hated.

*The sorrows being loosed.* The sense of this sentence seems to be, that when the Lord descended to the lower regions the sorrows of the punishments were loosed, because they could not touch him, but according to the Greek, in which it is written: *Loosing through him the sorrows of death, according as it was impossible that he should be held by it,* it is plain that through his descent the saints were freed from the places of the infernal regions; who, although they were in the bosom of Abraham, that is in the consolation of rest, yet were not wholly loosed from the sorrow of death or of hell, because they had not deserved to enter the joys of heaven, until that of the Prophet should come to pass: *In the blood of the testament thou hast led forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water ((Zach. V))*. For they were bound before they were led forth.

*I foresaw the Lord.* The voice of Christ exulting after the resurrection at the right hand. The left is the present life; the right, the eternal. *That I be not moved.* After the resurrection all things will be immovable. *And the tongue hath exulted.* Because rest after labour is given: for he laboured in the hope of eternal life. *Thou wilt not leave.* Let me not again be moved by the corruption of a repeated cross and death. *Thou hast made known to me.* I know that I shall always live. *Thou shalt fill me* with full gladness, that is, I shall not die again. *Because he is at the right hand.* The cause why he is not moved is that the Lord helps at the right hand, the left not prevailing. For if he be not at the right hand, the devil occupies that part, as is said of Judas: *And let the devil stand at his right hand ((Psal. CVIII))*.

*And hath exulted.* In the passion he said: *My soul is sorrowful even unto death ((Matth. XXVI))*: and he began to fear and to be heavy: that he might show himself true man in soul and body, and truly passible. But afterwards the soul and the tongue exulted, because by his passion the human race was to be saved.

*In hell.* It is agreed that the soul was not left in hell, which, when those had been taken away for whose sake he had descended, straightway returned to the things above, nor was the flesh corrupted, but glorified by a swift resurrection.

*Thou hast made known to me.* Not only are these things understood of him who, the fulness of divine power and wisdom being once received, destroyed death by himself, rising again to life; but also of the just who, the way of truth having been found through him, will return to life and will be gladdened, seeing his face: because that sight is above all things and is perfect beatitude.

notes.text: To thee — Thou dost not need me or my service, nor art capable of any advantage from it.

But — I bear a singular respect and love to all saints, for thy sake, whose friends and servants they are, and whose image they bear. This more properly agrees to David, than to Christ, whose goodness was principally designed for, and imparted to sinners.

Sorrows — Having shewed his affection to the servants of the true God, he now declares what an abhorrency he has for those that worship idols. Offerings - In which the Gentiles used sometimes to drink part of the blood of their sacrifices. Names - Of those other gods mentioned before.

The Lord — I rejoice in God as my portion, and desire no better, no other felicity. Cup - The portion which is put into my cup, as the ancient manner was in feasts, where each had his portion of meat, and of wine allotted to him. Lot - My inheritance divided to me by lot, as the custom then was.
Lines — My portion, which was measured with lines. Are fallen - In a land flowing with milk and honey, and above all, blessed with the presence and knowledge of God.

The Lord — Hath inspired that wisdom into me, by which I have chosen the Lord for my portion, and am so fully satisfied with him. Reins - My inward thoughts and affections, being inspired and moved by the Holy Spirit. Instruct - Direct me how to please God, and put my whole trust in him. Night - Even when others are asleep, my mind is working upon God, and improving the silence and solitude of holy meditations.

I have set — I have always presented him to my mind, as my witness and judge, as my patron and protector. Hitherto David seems to have spoken with respect to himself, but now he is transported by the spirit of prophecy, and carried above himself, to speak as a type of Christ, in whom this and the following verses were truly accomplished. Christ as man did always set his father's will and glory before him. Right-hand - To strengthen, protect, assist, and comfort me: as this assistance of God was necessary to Christ as man. Moved - Though the archers shoot grievously at me, and both men and devils seek my destruction, and God sets himself against me as an enemy, yet I am assured he will deliver me out of all my distresses.

My glory — My tongue, which is a man's glory and privilege, above all other living creatures. Rejoiceth - Declares my inward joy. For this word signifies not so much eternal joy, as the outward demonstrations of it. My flesh - My body shall quietly rest in the grave. Shall rest - in confident assurance of its incorruption there, and of its resurrection to an immortal life: the flesh or body is in itself, but a dead lump of clay; yet hope is here ascribed to it figuratively, as it is to the brute creatures, Rom. viii, 19.

Hell — In the state of the dead. Holy one - Me thy holy son, whom thou hast sanctified and sent into the world. It is peculiar to Christ, to be called the holy one of God. To see - To be corrupted or putrefied in the grave, as the bodies of others are.

Life — Thou wilt raise me from the grave, and conduct me to the place and state of everlasting felicity. Presence - In that heavenly paradise, where thou art gloriously present, where thou dost clearly and fully discover the light of thy countenance; whereas in this life thou hidest thy face and shewest us only thy back-parts. Right-hand - Which he mentions as a place of the greatest honour, the place where the saints are placed at the last day, and where Christ himself is said to sit, chap. cx, 1. Pleasures - All our joys are empty and defective: But in heaven there is fulness of joy. Our pleasures here are transient and momentary; but those at God's right hand are pleasures forevermore. For they are the pleasures of immortal souls, in the enjoyment of an eternal God. David appealing to God for his integrity, begs for defense against his enemies, ver. 1-9. Describes their wickedness, ver. 10- 12. Prays for deliverance from them, and rests in hope, ver. 13-15. A prayer of David.

glossa.text: *The inscription of a title.* ((CASS.)) This title is taken from the Gospel, not from the Old Testament. What the title noted, that is, victory and kingdom, belongs to Christ, and that is what is treated of here.

*Preserve me,* etc. The second psalm, which touches briefly on the passion and the resurrection; first, Christ, showing the one nature of man, asks to be preserved, saying that all that he endured has been brought through to the glory of his inheritance. ((AUG.)) Christ speaks here according to his manhood, of whom the royal title stood out in the passion: *Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.--Of my goods,* etc. ((CASS.)) If God has no need of the goods of Christ the man, but Christ the man has all things from him, the arrogance of men is overthrown, and the heresy of the Pelagians, who think that anything is done by their own good powers.

*To the saints who are in the land. ((Ibid.))* Christ has now set out how he prayed; he now tells what good things God did for him. ((AUG.)) *To the saints,* etc., *as far as* and power that I might rise again.

*He hath made wonderful.* ((CASS.)) As if to say, these things I said to the Lord: but the Lord made them wonderful, that is, he made my wills wonderful; and they are wonderful in that those who obey them become heavenly out of earthly.
*They are multiplied. ((Ibid.))* Whereby he made them wonderful, etc., *as far as* which sound together in one note, by which his wills are shown.

*The portion of my inheritance.* ((AUG.)) Let others choose other things, etc., *as far as* but those who choose God as their portion. ((CASS.)) Or, *the Lord* is the *portion,* that is, the share and the reward, *of my inheritance,* that is, of the saints. And *the portion of my cup,* that is, the wage of the passion. For the inheritance belongs to the Gentiles, the cup to the passion, which when drunk gives resurrection. But let no one think himself an heir save he that is illustrious.

*The lines,* etc. ((Ibid.)) As it were by lot, in which is the divine election, as the lot also fell upon Matthias, and each man takes according to his own measure. *In goodly places.* That is, among the saints.

*I will bless the Lord. ((Ibid.))* He gives thanks to the Father for understanding, and for the passion, in which by his favour he conquers, and for the resurrection, and for confession; and these are the things through which the inheritance is restored, so that he is king of the Jews, as the title says. *Understanding,* etc. ((AUG.)) Whereby this inheritance can be seen and possessed. *Moreover,* etc. That is, above understanding. *Even till night,* etc. That is, till death, he hath instructed me, that is, my lower part, the assumption of flesh, that he might drive out the darknesses of mortality which that understanding does not have, because for them it could neither be troubled nor fail. *My reins.* From whom according to the flesh I came forth, namely my kindred: they have chided me with injuries, with temptation and with passion.
*I set the Lord before me. ((Ibid.))* From this draw an example, whereby sins may be shunned: for he who always beholds God with the keen edge of the mind is not bowed down by sins.

notes.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — His Father, with respect to his divine nature; his God, with respect to his human. Who hath regenerated us to a living hope - An hope which implies true spiritual life, which revives the heart, and makes the soul lively and vigourous. By the resurrection of Christ - Which is not only a pledge of ours, but a part of the purchase price. It has also a close connection with our rising from spiritual death, that as he liveth, so shall we live with him. He was acknowledged to be the Christ, but usually called Jesus till his resurrection; then he was also called Christ.

To an inheritance — For if we are sons, then heirs. Incorruptible - Not like earthly treasures. Undefiled - Pure and holy, incapable of being itself defiled, or of being enjoyed by any polluted soul. And that fadeth not away - That never decays in its value, sweetness, or beauty, like all the enjoyments of this world, like the garlands of leaves or flowers, with which the ancient conquerors were wont to be crowned. Reserved in heaven for you - Who "by patient continuance in welldoing, seek for glory and honour and immortality."

Who are kept — The inheritance is reserved; the heirs are kept for it. By the power of God - Which worketh all in all, which guards us against all our enemies. Through faith - Through which alone salvation is both received and retained. Ready to be revealed - That Rev. is made in the last day. It was more and more ready to be revealed, ever since Christ came.

Wherein — That is, in being so kept. Ye even now greatly rejoice, though now for a little while - Such is our whole life, compared to eternity. If need be - For it is not always needful. If God sees it to be the best means for your spiritual profit. Ye are in heaviness - Or sorrow; but not in darkness; for they still retained both faith, 1 Pe i, 5, hope, and love; yea, at this very time were rejoicing with joy unspeakable, 1 Pe i, 8.

That the trial of your faith — That is, your faith which is tried. Which is much more precious than gold - For gold, though it bear the fire, yet will perish with the world. May be found - Though it doth not yet appear. Unto praise - From God himself. And honour - From men and angels. And glory - Assigned by the great Judge.
Having not seen — In the flesh.
Receiving — Now already. Salvation - From all sin into all holiness, which is the qualification for, the forerunner and pledge of, eternal salvation.

glossa.text: *He hath regenerated. ((Bed.))* Whereas by our own merits we had been begotten unto death, etc., *as far as* that through cleanness you may be heavens and the seat of God.

*Incorruptible.* The soul is not naturally incorruptible, but by the grace of God, through faith and justice, it is perfected incorruptible in respect of the understanding. *In you.* He who gave to you that believe the power to become the sons of God has placed in you that perseverance by which you may receive the inheritance in the heavens, because he who has not kept the discipline of the Father does not merit his inheritance.

*In the power.* No one by the power of his own liberty is able to be kept in good things, unless he from whom you have the beginning of a good action bring it to perfection. Labour out of faith through faith, being about to come unto eternal salvation, which, even if it does not now appear, is nevertheless prepared to be revealed, if we shall have been prepared.
*Now, if it be needful.* If, that is, although it be needful. Or, *if it be needful to be made sorrowful,* let us not fail.

*That the trial,* etc., *unto praise.* When the judge, praising your faith, shall say: *And you gave me to eat,* etc ((Matth. XXV)).

*More precious than gold. ((Bed.))* The patience of the saints is compared to gold, etc., *as far as* whence he also subjoins: *May it be found,* etc.

 *Unto praise.* That you may be praiseworthy and glorious through constancy *in the revelation,* that is, in the day of judgment, when it shall be revealed of how great power God is. *And honour,* that it may be said to you: *Come, ye blessed of my Father ((Matth. XXV))*.

*The salvation of souls.* This salvation is much to be loved, because concerning this salvation they sought much, when or in what order eternal salvation should come to the world; whence it is said: *Many prophets and kings have wished to see the things which you see, and have not seen them ((Matth. XIII))*.

notes.text: Mark xvi, 14 Luke xxiv, 36.

Peace be unto you — This is the foundation of the mission of a true Gospel minister, peace in his own soul, 2 Cor. iv, 1. As the Father hath sent me, so send I you - Christ was the apostle of the Father, Heb. iii, 1. Peter and the rest, the apostles of Christ.

He breathed on them — New life and vigour, and saith, as ye receive this breath out of my mouth, so receive ye the Spirit out of my fulness: the Holy Ghost influencing you in a peculiar manner, to fit you for your great embassy. This was an earnest of pentecost.

Whosoever sins ye remit — (According to the tenor of the Gospel, that is, supposing them to repent and believe) they are remitted, and whosoever sins ye retain (supposing them to remain impenitent) they are retained. So far is plain. But here arises a difficulty. Are not the sins of one who truly repents, and unfeignedly believes in Christ, remitted, without sacerdotal absolution? And are not the sins of one who does not repent or believe, retained even with it? What then does this commission imply? Can it imply any more than,

1. A power of declaring with authority the Christian terms of pardon; whose sins are remitted and whose retained? As in our daily form of absolution; and

2. A power of inflicting and remitting ecclesiastical censures? That is, of excluding from, and re-admitting into, a Christian congregation.
After eight days — On the next Sunday.

And Thomas said, My Lord and my God — The disciples had said, We have seen the Lord. Thomas now not only acknowledges him to be the Lord, as he had done before, and to be risen, as his fellow disciples had affirmed, but also confesses his Godhead, and that more explicitly than any other had yet done. And all this he did without putting his hand upon his side.
Jesus wrought many miracles, which are not written in this book — Of St. John, nor indeed of the other evangelists.
But these things are written that ye may believe — That ye may be confirmed in believing. Faith cometh sometimes by reading; though ordinarily by hearing.

glossa.text: *When therefore,* etc. This was done on the very day of the resurrection, on which Jesus appeared five times. First to Mary Magdalene, secondly to the same woman running with the others who wished to announce it to the disciples, thirdly to Peter, fourthly to Cleophas and his companion, fifthly to the disciples, the doors being shut, the two aforesaid having now returned.

*He shewed them his hands and his side.* After the resurrection the Lord showed in his body two contrary things: both what was palpable, of the same nature, that he might form them to faith, and what was incorruptible, of another glory, that he might invite them to the reward.

*He said therefore to them again. Peace be to you,* etc. He offers peace, who came for the sake of peace; he repeats it, that he may show that through his blood the things that are in heaven and the things that are on earth have been made peaceful.
*Receive ye the Holy Ghost. ((AUG.))* On earth the spirit is given that the neighbour may be loved; from heaven the Spirit is given that God may be loved.

*Whose sins you shall forgive.* Behold charity, which is poured into their hearts through the Holy Ghost. He forgives the sins of those who are partakers of him; of those who are not, he retains them. And therefore after he had said: *Receive ye the Holy Ghost,* he immediately subjoined: *Whose sins you shall forgive.*

*Now Thomas, one.* Not by chance, but by divine disposition was Thomas absent, and he did not believe what he heard; whence the Lord offered himself to him to be handled, because by his doubting, and by the proof made to him, it is now left to no one to doubt. *Who is called Didymus.* Didymus, that is, twin, because Thomas is doubtful; that is, an abyss: because by doubting he knew more deeply.
*He answered.* He was seeing and touching the man, and above this he believed him God, doubt being now removed, and he confessed him whom he did not see.

*Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed.* He does not say, thou hast touched, but, thou hast seen: because sight is in a manner the general sense, which is wont to be said of the other four. Perhaps he did not dare to touch; but by looking only, or even by touching, he believes.

*Blessed.* He commends the faith of the Gentiles, but he uses the past tense, as one who knew that what was to come was already done in his own predestination.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit. I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day […]
echoes.note: Formal, formula-marked citation ('this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel,' v.16) reproducing Joel 2:28-32 (LXX 3:1-5) at high verbal volume: pouring out the Spirit on all flesh, sons/daughters prophesying, young men visions, old men dreams, servants and handmaids, wonders in heaven and signs on earth, blood/fire/smoke, sun to darkness and moon to blood before the great day of the Lord, and whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved. Luke's 'in the last days' adapts Joel's 'afterward.' The anchor quotation of the chapter; maximal on all three auditable tests.

echoes.text: Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
echoes.note: The 'smoke' (kapnos) among the apocalyptic signs (v.19) may resonate with the smoke of Sinai where 'the mountain was wholly in smoke' at the theophany, reinforcing the Sinai-Pentecost frame. Low volume and the wording is governed by Joel; contested.

echoes.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: 'Before the great and notable day of the Lord' overlaps the Malachi expectation of the great and dreadful day of the LORD; the phrase is shared eschatological idiom that Joel and Malachi both carry. Faint and mediated through Joel; contested as an independent source.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

echoes.text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but Yahweh tests the hearts.
echoes.note: 'The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts' is the proverbial matrix for faith 'tested by fire... more precious than gold.' High thematic coherence; gold-tested-by-fire is a stock wisdom topos Peter applies to faith.

echoes.text: Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.
echoes.note: 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel' is the berakah doxology Peter Christianizes as 'Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.' Distinctive opening-blessing form recurring across the Psalter's book-seams.

echoes.text: Therefore David blessed Yahweh before all the assembly; and David said, “You are blessed, Yahweh, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.
echoes.note: David's 'Blessed are you, O LORD, the God of Israel our father' supplies both the eulogy form and the Father-language behind 1:3; coherent with the inheritance theme that follows (29:11-16).

echoes.text: Yahweh assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure. The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is my portion and my inheritance... a goodly heritage' reframes inheritance from land to God himself, the move behind an 'inheritance kept in heaven.' Thematic coherence high; the imperishable heavenly inheritance transposes the Levitical land-allotment.

echoes.text: I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them. I will say, ‘It is my people;’ and they will say, ‘Yahweh is my God.’”
echoes.note: 'I will refine them as one refines silver and test them as gold is tested,' set in an eschatological remnant-purification, supplies the trial-as-refinement frame of 1:6-7; verbal contact (refine/test, gold) plus eschatological coherence.

echoes.text: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come out like gold.
echoes.note: 'When he has tested me, I shall come forth as gold' is the closest first-person analogue: testing through suffering yielding vindicated, gold-like faith. Strong thematic coherence, moderate volume.

echoes.text: And having borne a little chastening, they will receive great good; Because God made trial of them, and found them worthy of himself. As gold in the furnace he proved them, And as a whole burnt offering he accepted them.
echoes.note: 'Having been disciplined a little... like gold in the furnace he tried them' joins brief affliction ('a little while', cf. 1:6) with gold-furnace testing of the righteous souls; strong thematic coherence with 1:6-9.

echoes.text: I heard, but I didn’t understand: then I said, my lord, what shall be the issue of these things? He said, Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
echoes.note: Daniel 'heard but did not understand' and sought the meaning, told the words were 'sealed until the time of the end'—the paradigm for prophets who 'searched diligently... what time the Spirit pointed to' (1:10-11). Distinctive prophet-seeks-yet-defers motif.

echoes.text: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.
echoes.note: 'According to your great mercy' echoes the Psalter's 'according to the abundance of your mercy'; low volume but a fixed liturgical collocation.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Aaron, “You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.
echoes.note: The priests have no land-inheritance because 'I am your portion and inheritance'; Peter's heavenly, unfading inheritance figurally fulfills this priestly pattern (cf. royal priesthood, 2:9). Figural, low verbal volume.

echoes.text: But the righteous live forever, And in the Lord is their reward, And the care for them with the Most High. Therefore will they receive the crown of royal dignity And the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand; Because with his right hand will he cover them, And with his arm will he shield them.
echoes.note: 'The righteous live forever... they will receive a glorious crown... from the Lord's hand' parallels the imperishable, heaven-reserved inheritance and the 'praise, glory, and honor' of 1:7; Second Temple thematic coherence.

echoes.text: [source text not in the World English Bible]
echoes.note: 'My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing... for gold is tested in the fire, and those found acceptable in the furnace of humiliation.' The fullest pre-Christian template: discipleship + fiery testing + gold + acceptance, mirroring 1:6-7. Second Temple recurrence and high thematic coherence.

echoes.text: Surely the Lord Yahweh will do nothing, unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets.
echoes.note: 'The Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets' undergirds 'to them it was revealed' that they served a later generation (1:12); thematic, low verbal volume.

echoes.text: After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities.
echoes.note: 'The sufferings of Christ and the glories that follow' (1:11) tracks the Servant's affliction-then-vindication arc (Isaiah 52:13-53:12); Peter's signature suffering/glory pattern, faint here but recurrent in the letter.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: Jesus 'breathed on them' and said 'Receive the Holy Spirit' — the verb (enephysesen, LXX of Gen 2:7) directly evokes God breathing the breath of life into Adam's nostrils so he became a living being. John presents the Spirit-impartation as new creation/new Adam; very high Volume given the rare shared verb and high Coherence with the Gospel's creation theology.

echoes.text: Then he said to me, Prophesy to the wind, prophesy, son of man, and tell the wind, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
echoes.note: 'Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live' stands behind Jesus breathing Spirit into the disciples after the resurrection. Ezekiel's vivified corpses give the scene its resurrection-and-Spirit valence; high Coherence and shared breath/Spirit (ruach/pneuma) vocabulary reinforce the Genesis 2:7 figure.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
echoes.note: The risen Jesus' threefold greeting 'Peace be to you' (20:19,21,26) functions as the eschatological enactment of the Aaronic priestly blessing 'the LORD lift up his countenance on you and give you peace.' Medium Volume (shared 'peace') with strong Coherence as the resurrected high-priestly Lord blesses his gathered people.

echoes.text: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
echoes.note: The authority to forgive or retain sins ('he shall open, and no one shall shut; he shall shut, and no one shall open') parallels the key-of-the-house-of-David grant of binding/loosing power. The remit-or-retain antithesis matches the open/shut structure of the oracle; medium confidence on the structural rather than verbal link.

echoes.text: Because he was ignorant of him that moulded him, And of him that inspired into him an active soul, And breathed into him a vital spirit.
echoes.note: 'He failed to know the one who formed him and inspired him with an active soul and breathed into him a living spirit' restates Gen 2:7 in Second-Temple idiom, evidencing the availability of the breath-of-life motif John reworks. Deuterocanonical witness rather than a direct source.

echoes.text: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
echoes.note: 'I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake' grounds the forgiveness of sins as a divine prerogative now delegated to the disciples (20:23). Faint background highlighting that sin-forgiveness is God's act, sharpening the Christological claim.

echoes.text: Wake up! Rise up to defend me, my God! My Lord, contend for me!
echoes.note: Thomas' confession 'My Lord and my God!' (20:28) reproduces the psalmist's vocative 'my God and my Lord' (LXX Ps 34:23: ho theos mou kai ho kyrios mou). The unusual paired address gives high Volume; John climaxes the Gospel by directing to Jesus the cry the psalmist directs to YHWH.

echoes.text: But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
echoes.note: Thomas addresses Jesus with the divine titles 'Lord... God' that the psalter repeatedly couples ('you, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious'), reinforcing the deliberate transfer of YHWH-language to the risen Christ. Supporting Recurrence behind the primary Ps 35:23 allusion.

echoes.text: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed' (20:29) coheres with 'the righteous shall live by his faith,' the OT charter of faith-not-sight. Thematic rather than verbal; faint and one of several wisdom/faith backgrounds.

echoes.text: Yahweh answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it. For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'These are written, that you may believe' enacts the prophetic command 'Write the vision; make it plain... it awaits its appointed time,' grounding the inscribed witness-for-faith in the OT theology of the written vision that calls for belief. Medium Coherence with the Gospel's purpose statement; verbal contact is on the writing-for-faith motif.

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. Those who are wise shall […]
echoes.note: The notion of words 'written in this book' so that the faithful 'may have life' faintly recalls Daniel's sealed book and those 'found written in the book' who awake to everlasting life. Low Volume; offered as a faint life-through-the-book resonance.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The confessional goal 'that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God' draws on the royal-messianic decree 'You are my Son,' the OT title-cluster (Messiah / Son of God) John affirms. Background to the titulature rather than a quotation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The doors were locked, and fear sat with the disciples.
Jesus came and stood among them.
He showed them his hands and his side.
Peace be with you, he said.
Thomas touched the wounds and believed.
My Lord and my God!
Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come in, you who have bolted the doors against the dark; the room is full of fear, and still he stands among us.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Hear him breathe over us the word we cannot say for ourselves: Peace. Peace be with you.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He holds out his wounded hands to every doubt, to every Thomas who needs to touch and see.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Blessed are you who have not seen, and yet have come to believe.
Christ is risen, alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Behind locked doors, fear kept us; Jesus came and stood among us.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He breathed on us his peace.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
He showed his wounds, and our doubt became worship.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
Blessed are those who believe. Come, let us worship.
Christ is risen, alleluia!
